info.title: InstaCloud API — Project level
info.description:
Endpoints under `/projects/{projectId}`: branches, services, deploys, secrets, databases, storage, cron, observability, governance. Callable with any token whose binding covers the project.

Generated from the platform's own OpenAPI document (https://api.instacloud.com/openapi.json); see the [API overview](/reference/api/overview) for authentication and token scopes.

**Token scope:** `account` · `org` · `project` — read-only tokens refused (not a GET).

Write a batch of user secrets, then redeploy the compute services those values reach, one deploy per service. Entries are reported written individually and services are reported deployed, started, skipped or failed individually, because the writes commit before the deploys run and a failed deploy never rolls a value back. `skipDeploy` writes without deploying. `excludeFromDeploy` drops services the caller is deploying itself; `deployOnly` names the services to deploy and ignores derivation, which is how a failed deploy is retried with no entries. A rename writes no env, so it deploys nothing on its own and needs no `deploy` grant — a batch that both renames and writes still deploys, for the write. Gated on what the body contains: `secrets.write` for any set or delete, `service.rename` for a rename, `deploy` only for what can actually deploy. A project-scoped entry is authorized against every branch, since that is where its value lands. Deploying a stopped service starts it. A suspended service is skipped instead of deployed: a deploy would invalidate the RAM snapshot suspension exists to preserve, so it is left untouched and reported with reason `suspended`.

get.description:
**Token scope:** `account` · `org` · `project` — read-only tokens allowed.

A long-lived `text/event-stream`. Each `audit` event carries the new row's id, projectId, branchId, source, kind and createdAt — never its payload; read that from `GET /projects/{projectId}/events`. Send the last event `id` back as `Last-Event-ID` to have what followed replayed (the opening frame carries an `id` too, so an idle stream can resume); the replay overlaps, so an event can arrive twice — dedupe by its `id`. A `reset` event means the gap could not be replayed in full (or the server lost its own subscription): refetch every view. A `live` event (projectId, branchId, kind; no `id`) signals progress that records no audit row — a service coming online, a build or deploy changing stage, a template run advancing — so refetch what its kind names; it is never replayed. The server ends each stream after a few minutes; reconnect with the cursor.

parameters.name: last-event-id
parameters.description: the `id` of the last event received; what followed it is replayed first

parameters.description: service group/name (default: the branch's sole matching service, else 'default')

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: unix seconds — window start; compute pages the provider log cursor from here (~7-day retention)

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: unix seconds — window end (default now)

Restart a compute service by re-submitting the image reference recorded on it, against a freshly resolved env bundle. This is how a changed secret or binding reaches a running machine, and how a machine that is up but wedged gets cycled (`start` only wakes a machine that is DOWN — it no-ops on one that is already started). It asks for no new version and no new spec, but it does not pin a digest: a service recorded against a MOVING tag (`app:latest`) gets whatever that tag resolves to now, exactly as a redeploy of the same tag would. Requires desired_state 'running': a stopped or suspended service is brought back with `start`, which also re-enables auto-wake. All plans. Gated under `deploy`, like the deploy route it shares its pipeline with — a policy denying deploys denies this too, and `start`/`stop` stay ungated for cycling a wedged machine without one.

get.description:
**Token scope:** `account` · `org` · `project` — read-only tokens allowed.

Poll a template deployment: status, current step, per-service URLs, and the failure log tail.

bearerAuth.description: Session access JWT or an API token (`insta_<prefix>_<secret>`).

requested_by.description: Better Auth user id (opaque string, not a UUID)

decided_by.description: Better Auth user id (opaque string, not a UUID)

action.description: the gated action, or a comma-joined compound set — prefer `actions`

url.description: the console page where a project admin reviews this request

actor_user_id.description: Better Auth user id (opaque string, not a UUID)

BuildHistoryEntry.description: A source build and deployment attempt for a compute service.

nextCursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor. No cursor means the current page is the tail, not that a running build has finished logging.

ComputeProvider.description: Compute plane actually backing a compute resource, derived from its provider_ref rather than its kind. Absent when it cannot be determined from the row — clients must then assert no provider rather than assume one from `kind`.

required.description: Installed by the platform and cannot be disabled

collected.description: false = suspended instance or provider without the capability; sections are structural zeros

lastVacuum.description: last manual or auto vacuum (UTC); omitted = never

note.description: present when the provider serves no insight at all

storageSize.description: DEPRECATED alias of volumeSize — dropped next release

storageGiB.description: DEPRECATED alias of volumeGib — dropped next release

cpuMilli.description: current cpu ceiling in millicores (2000 = 2 vCPU)

cap.description: this plan's maximum for the ceilings — render sliders with their plan-limit markers. These are the caller's own tier caps and they move with the plan (and with env overrides per deployment), so read them from THIS field rather than assuming a tier's numbers; the parenthetical example that used to live here said 'pro 4 vCPU/4Gi/10Gi' and was stale on all three by the time anyone noticed.

cacheHitRatio.description: 0..1; blks_hit/(blks_hit+blks_read). Omitted when unmeasurable (suspended instance or no cache traffic yet)

state.description: provider instance state (e.g. running/suspended) when known

serverVersion.description: postgres server version, e.g. "16.14", when measured

activeBranchId.description: the project default branch id AFTER restore (changes on finalize_restore)

type.description: provider backup type, such as full or incr

tags.description: provider backup tags; tags.type=manual marks user-created manual backups

sourceCleared.description: the service deployed from a repo before this call; that connection is removed and the source is now `image`

costUsd.description: quantity × unit price for this dimension in the window

service.description: the compute service this hostname serves; each hostname of a domain can serve a different one

sampleIntervalSeconds.description: Source sampling interval in seconds, independent of the requested chart step.

note.description: present when a provider can't serve the request (e.g. DB metrics)

op.description: Neutral logical action id, e.g. "service.add" — NOT an operationId or a CLI/MCP tool name; each client maps it to its own surface.

args.description: Suggested, flat named arguments; "<placeholder>"s where a value is unknown.

gated.description: True if the action passes a governance gate.

owner_user_id.description: Better Auth user id (opaque string, not a UUID)

cpuUnmeasuredApps.description: apps excluded from the cpu ratio for lack of a reading

ramUnmeasuredApps.description: apps excluded from the ram ratio for lack of a reading

cpuSuspectApps.description: apps excluded because actual exceeded allocation — impossible, so the stored rows are wrong

ramSuspectApps.description: apps excluded because actual exceeded allocation — impossible, so the stored rows are wrong

cpuUnmeteredApps.description: apps with no cpu metering rows at all — the ratio was computed over a smaller fleet than the real one

ramUnmeteredApps.description: apps with no ram metering rows at all — the ratio was computed over a smaller fleet than the real one

byService.description: the same window and the same money split by service — deleted services included, plus one unattributed bucket where the service is unrecoverable. Sums to totalCostUsd. A postgres lineage ROOT is attributed to its origin service, so a forked environment’s database cost lands on the service it was forked from.

status.description: detached: every service its hostnames named is gone — attach it again

locked.description: the registrar transfer lock: while it is on, no other registrar can pull the domain away. Turn it off to move the domain out. What the last write reported, or what registration asked for — nothing reads it back

nameservers.description: what the registrar holds. Empty means never written — only a nameserver write fills it in

delegated.description: the zone is answered by nameservers InstaCloud cannot write to (custody `foreign`), so nothing published resolves and an attach is refused. A MANAGED delegation reads false: the platform still publishes there

custody.description: who answers the domain's zone: the registrar's own nameservers, a managed InstaCloud zone (delegated, still platform-published), or somewhere the platform cannot write

transferLockExpiresAt.description: ICANN 60-day lock after registration: no transfer out before this, whatever `locked` says

Resource.description: Public view of a provisioned resource (no credential material).

name.description: compute group label for a compute resource (kind=fly | insta-compute)

ref.description: Non-credential identifiers (e.g. fly url, bucket name, database project id)

allocated.description: the ceiling that was billed, in `unit`. NULL means no allocation was recorded in this window — not that nothing was allocated.

actual.description: what the app actually consumed, same unit. NULL means not measured in this window — not zero.

utilisation.description: actual / allocated; null when either side is unknown

suspect.description: actual exceeds allocation, which is physically impossible — the stored rows are wrong. Excluded from totals.

unmetered.description: the app exists but the collector produced no rows at all for it in this window — neither allocation nor reading. Worse than an absent reading: nothing bounds how much of the fleet is missing.

name.description: env-var name more than one service defines, so a flat bundle cannot attribute a value to it

services.description: "<type>/<name>" of every service that defines it; a since-removed holder appears as its service id

SecretsBundle.description: env-var name → decrypted value (e.g. DATABASE_URL, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, ...)

Service.description: A project-level service (postgres | storage | compute | redis | mysql | mongodb).

spec.description: compute: {cpu_kind,cpus,memory_mb}; postgres: sized by its instance ceiling (cpuMilli/memoryMib)

always_on.description: compute only — true (the platform default for new compute services): machines never scale to zero; false: idle machines suspend and wake on request. Billing is actual usage either way.

websocket.description: compute only — the app speaks WebSocket, so its machines carry connections-based concurrency and a 512 MB guest floor. Re-asserted by any redeploy given no flag, including restart. null: never recorded.

public.description: storage only — bucket(s) served with anonymous public-read

image.description: compute only — container image currently run

port.description: compute/managed database — compute image port, or the private database TCP port

start_command.description: Runtime startup override via sh -c; null uses the built image default. Stored as readable service settings.

volume_applied_mount_path.description: Last successfully confirmed Compute mount path; null means unknown, not proof of a changed path.

volume_mount_path.description: Compute volume mount path; null or omitted means /data for legacy volumes. Changes apply on deployment.

volume_gib.description: compute/managed database — size (whole Gi) of the persistent data volume; null = no volume. Compute can attach/grow via PUT .../volume; managed databases are platform-managed in v1

pg_version.description: postgres only — the Postgres MAJOR version the service runs (e.g. 16), known before the instance is ever connected to or woken. Pick client tooling (pg_dump/pg_restore/psql) of the same major. null: never recorded (a legacy row). The exact server_version of a RUNNING instance is on GET .../database/metrics

template_deployment_id.description: the template deployment that created this service (survives branch clones); null for services created directly

template_modified.description: true once the service was reconfigured away from its template-deployed spec

template_code.description: the template this service was deployed from; null for services created directly, and for one whose deployment record has been pruned

template_logo_url.description: the template's mark, absolute and pinned to the commit that published it; null when the template is not in the registry (or carries no logo). Joined live rather than stored, because a republish moves it

ServiceBuild.description: One build → image → deploy attempt of a service source (one per commit per source).

source_id.description: the service source that queued it; null once that source was disconnected

repo_binding_id.description: DEPRECATED — set only on builds queued before sources existed; null for every new build

ServiceSource.description: Where a compute service’s running image comes from: an image somebody deployed (type=image, the absence of a connected source) or a connected repository (type=github).

image.description: type=image — the image the service runs; null when nothing has been deployed yet

branch.description: the repo branch this service tracks; defaults to the repo’s default branch

root_dir.description: subdirectory to build from (monorepo); null = repo root. Also decides which pushes deploy this service: the build context is this directory, so a push that changed nothing under it is skipped

watch_paths.description: include list of gitignore patterns, matched against paths relative to the repository root (not to root_dir); a push deploys this service only when it changed a matching path. null/absent falls back to the root-directory rule: a service with root_dir deploys when a push changed something under it, one building from the repo root deploys on every push

auto_deploy.description: a push to `branch` rebuilds and redeploys; always false for a public repo (no App, no webhooks)

public.description: connected as a public repo, without a GitHub App installation

build_command.description: custom build command for source builds without a Dockerfile; null uses automatic detection

last_build.description: the newest build of this service (null before the first)

ServiceSourceSummary.description: compute only — where the running image comes from: an image somebody deployed (type=image) or a connected repository (type=github). Full resource: GET /projects/{id}/services/{serviceId}/source

branch.description: the repo branch this service tracks

auto_deploy.description: a push to `branch` rebuilds and redeploys the service

serviceId.description: null for the unattributed bucket: spend with no live service to name — its environment was deleted, or the resource predates service attribution (pre-0010, never backfilled). NOT spend of zero

type.description: postgres | storage | compute | redis | mysql | mongodb

status.description: 'deleted' for a service that is gone but still owns history

branch.description: the environment it belonged to; null for the unattributed bucket

TemplateDeployment.description: One server-side template deployment run and its progress.

status.description: partial = some services came up healthy, others failed — created resources are kept either way

step.description: the pipeline step the run is currently on (or stopped at)

region.description: InstaCloud region slug every service of this deployment was created in. Deployments recorded before regions were recorded read as the platform default.

name.description: the service's actual name on the branch, which is the manifest's name only for the first copy — a second deployment of the same template into the same branch names its services <name>-2 and leaves the first copy alone

logsTail.description: container log tail captured when a service never became healthy
